prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want a specific name or a short list of local companies, or would you prefer guidance on how to find and vet contractors yourself? A few quick questions first will let me give the most useful recommendations:

- What kind of work is it (small repair, full bathroom/kitchen remodel, room addition, roofing, siding, general handyman)?
- Rough budget and timeline?
- Do you need someone licensed/insured, union, or who works on VA/FHA loans, etc.?
- Do you prefer a local Joplin-based contractor only?

If you want a quick, practical plan right away, here are reliable steps and resources to find a good contractor in Joplin, plus a vetting checklist you can use immediately.

Where to look
- Google Maps reviews (search “home remodel contractor Joplin, MO”)
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), Houzz, HomeAdvisor — for reviews and project photos
- Better Business Bureau (bbb.org) — complaints and ratings
- Nextdoor and local Facebook community groups — real-neighbor recommendations
- Local building department in Joplin (to see permit history and whether contractors pull permits)
- Word-of-mouth: neighbors, friends, local real estate agents

How to vet contractors (quick checklist)
- Verify liability insurance and worker’s comp — ask for certificates and call the carrier to confirm.
- Ask for 3 recent references (same project type) and call them; ask to see finished work if possible.
- Check online reviews and BBB complaints; watch for how complaints were resolved.
- Confirm licensing if required for your project (ask the city/county if a specific license is needed).
- Get at least 3 written estimates with line-item breakdowns (materials, labor, permits).
- Make sure they will obtain required permits and schedule inspections.
- Ask about warranties on workmanship and materials, and what’s covered.
- Get a written contract with scope, materials, timeline, total price, payment schedule, change-order process, and cleanup responsibilities.
- Avoid large upfront cash-only payments (common safe practice: deposit 10–30%, progress payments, final payment after inspection/approval).
- Ask about subcontractors they use and whether they carry insurance and sign lien waivers.

Questions to ask each contractor
- How long have you been working in Joplin/southwest Missouri?
- Can you provide three local references and photos of similar completed projects?
- Who will be on site — owner, foreman, subcontractors?
- What is the project schedule and expected completion date?
- How do you handle change orders and unforeseen issues?
- What permits are required and who pulls them?
- What warranties do you provide?

Red flags to avoid
- No written contract or vague scope
- Requests for large cash-only deposits
- Poor or no references; lots of unresolved BBB complaints
- Pressure to sign immediately or “special today” pricing
- Unwillingness to provide certificates of insurance

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short message/email you can send to contractors asking the right questions
- Help you evaluate 3 bids if you paste them here
- (If you want a local list) compile a shortlist of Joplin-area contractors — tell me the project type and I’ll prepare names and what to ask each one

Which would you prefer?
